headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared file-based workflows; Plandex’s write access can also cascade OCR errors into unsafe code changes.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR ingests document/image content and Plandex reads project files from a shared workspace, so malicious text embedded in OCR output can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks any documented provenance or isolation between A’s extracted text and B’s planner inputs, making injection plausible in default file-based workflows.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is written into a file that Plandex reads as task context
IF Plandex processes OCR text without provenance tagging or instruction filtering
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Plandex consumes OCR output
Prefix OCR output with a non-executable data wrapper
Store OCR artifacts in a separate directory from prompts
Disable auto-apply for any plan derived from OCR text
requires-engineering: add provenance labels from OCR to downstream planner inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Plandex reads and writes project files and sends context to a model provider or Plandex Cloud. If sensitive document content is OCR’d into the shared workspace, B can transmit it onward. A does not itself show secret handling, but the pair still creates a default leakage path through file-based handoff.
conditions: IF documents or images containing sensitive data are OCR’d into Plandex-visible files
IF Plandex forwards those files or derived context to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive OCR inputs outside Plandex workspaces
Redact documents before OCR
Use a local-only model backend for Plandex
Restrict Plandex to a dedicated low-sensitivity project directory
requires-engineering: enforce content classification before API egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress; PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs. In a shared project directory, B can overwrite or commit artifacts that A produced, and the pair has no documented locking or coordination. That makes concurrent mutation of the same workspace dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or git repository
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while PaddleOCR is still producing outputs
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate directory
Disable Plandex auto-apply
Serialize access with a manual lock file
Commit OCR outputs before planner edits
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents and images, and Plandex is a coding agent that can turn that text into shell or git actions. Because Plandex’s review-then-apply flow still allows optional auto-apply, OCR mistakes or injected text can cascade into irreversible code changes or commands without strong verification.
conditions: IF OCR output is used as authoritative input for a plan
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled or human review is skipped
mitigations: Require human review of every plan derived from OCR
Compare OCR text against the source document image
Disable auto-apply
Limit Plandex to read-only analysis for OCR-derived tasks
requires-engineering: add verification against source artifacts before execution

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR is open-source document processing with no stated residency or retention constraints, while Plandex stores project files and may send context to Plandex Cloud or a model provider. The pair does not show a specific regulated-data mismatch, but if sensitive documents are OCR’d into Plandex’s cloud path, compliance obligations can diverge.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through Plandex Cloud or another third-party model provider
IF the documents include data subject to residency or retention rules
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of cloud-backed runs
Use self-hosted or local-only inference
Document retention expectations before processing
Separate regulated and non-regulated projects
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
